extracted.intended_audience: KIPO patent examiners and patent applicants (Korea)
extracted.subtask_description: Official KIPO examination procedures and standards covering citation formats, requests for extensions/shortenings, written arguments, amendment handling, requests for reference documents, additional searches, and deferral/extension of examination. Guidance is for examiners deciding patentability and for applicants responding to office actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of description when citing publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Order of description when citing publications is as follows; Name of Author, Title of Thesis, Title of Publication. Location of Publication: Publisher. Publication Date, Number of Volumes, Number of Issues, Page No.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Punctuation rules: Name of Author, Title of Thesis, and Title of Publication shall be discerned using a period (.), Location of Publication and Publisher is distinguished using a colon (:). Put a period (.) after Publisher. Others are divided using a comma (,).

rubrics_metrics.name: Title and abbreviation rules for publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Title of publication is generally not stated in abbreviations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title of publication is written in italics. For a publication translated into foreign languages, write original language with Korean in parentheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volume/issue and date formatting for periodicals
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of volumes and issues are stated as 'Volume oo, No.oo'. For English publications, 'Vol. oo, No. oo'. Where publication date can substitute a number of volume, the statement of volume and issue numbers can be omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication date refers to date inscribed on documents; if day not inscribed, month/year is sufficient. For unclear publication date, state the documents with explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page numbering format in citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Pages in publications of periodicals or non-periodicals are indicated with consecutive number of the concerned issue and cited using 'pp' in front of numeral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where citation involves plural consecutive pages use hyphen (-) between first and last page; use comma (,) for discontinuous pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book citation order and details
rubrics_metrics.description: Name of Author (or Name of Editor). Book Title. Location of Publication: Publisher. Publication Date, Number of Volume, No. of Edition, and No. of Page is the order for book citation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Book title is italicized. For a translated book include Name of Translator after author/editor. Number of edition can be omitted if not indicated. For books published in Korea, location of publication is omitted. Page numbers stated with 'pp.'; plural pages follow periodical rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citing parts of a publication for grounds of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a part of publication is cited for the grounds for rejection, page number or drawing number shall be included in parenthesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example formats are provided (journal entry, book entry with pp. o).

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of electronic documents
rubrics_metrics.description: When citing electronic documents searched from CD-ROM, the internet, or on-line DB, state the general information of the cited documents along with types of search medium (state in a brace), search date (state in a brace after the publication date) and search site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Title. Organization. [online], February 2001, [Search on July 15, 2010], Internet: <URL: ...>.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension/reduction principle for designated periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Commissioner of KIPO or an examiner may, upon request shorten or extend the period (designated period), or extend the period ex officio, and shall decide so that it does not unlawfully violate interests of the interested parties involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General principle governs all designated periods for patent procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions for substantive examination — request frequency and minimum unit
rubrics_metrics.description: The extension of the designated period pursuant to Article 16 of the Enforcement Decree of the Patent Act can be requested once or twice a month. Where a request for extension period is less than one month, it is regarded as one month extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except for period designated for written-argument submission, a request for period extension is deemed approved on its request date, but an examiner may partially approve or disapprove remaining period if it unlawfully violates interests; disapproved remaining period must be notified by warning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions for written-argument submission — deemed approval and review
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a request for extending the period designated for written argument submission is filed and the expiry date in the extended period is within four months from the original expiry date, the request is deemed to be approved on its request date. If beyond the prescribed period, examiner reviews request reasons and approves if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If extended expiry date is later than the period designated for extension request, examiner approves up to expiry of the designated-for-extension request and reviews remaining period. After approval, examiner issues written notification explaining purport and informs that additional extension can be requested by petition with additional reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable reasons for extension of written-argument period
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of acceptable reasons for approval of extension include: (i) applicant elects an agent for first time or changes/discharges an agent within a month from expiry; (ii) change of applicants within a month when new applicants added; (iii) receipt of foreign patent office outcomes within two months from expiry and submission of those outcomes; (iv) delivery of the written ground for rejection delayed more than one month; (v) original or later-filed application is pending on a trial or litigation; (vi) necessary for testing or evaluation of test results related to ground for rejection; (vii) other unavoidable cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the period extension request is filed by a third party, reasons (i)–(v) are not admitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for period extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Where fees for period extension request are not paid, an examiner shall request an applicant to pay within a time limit. If paid within the time limit, the extension request is regarded as valid; if not, the extension request is invalidated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This guideline applies for both statutory period and period designated for substantive examination. Fees shall be refunded where a request for period extension is rejected or where request is filed after the designated period and returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formality-examination extension limits and approval
rubrics_metrics.description: The period designated for amendment according to Article 46 of the Patent Act can be extended several times for the minimum period of a month or longer upon request, but the period available for extension shall not exceed more than four months in total.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a request does not exceed four months and fee paid, the request is deemed approved upon filing. For a four-month extension, a forewarning 'no further extension will be approved afterward' must be attached to the written approval; further extension requests will be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortening designated period and appeal extension
rubrics_metrics.description: The period designated for a patent-related procedure can be shortened according to request and is deemed to have expired as of the submission date of the shortening request form or written amendment. Any person can request to extend the period for requesting an appeal trial against decision to reject a patent only once and for up to 30 days; number and period may be further extended for persons in difficult-to-access areas subject to review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a written amendment for specification or drawing(s) is submitted after the designated period, it shall be returned due to overdue submission; amendments as to formalities are admitted any time before invalidation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner review of written arguments and amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a written argument is submitted along with an amendment, an examiner shall review both the argument and the amendment in depth and determine whether the notified grounds for rejection can be overcome based on such argument and amendment. Where only a written argument is submitted without an amendment, an examiner shall consider sufficiently the argument to determine whether the grounds for rejection can be overcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a written argument insists matters to be amended but no amendment is submitted, examination shall be made on the description and claims; where there is discrepancy between argued amendments and actual amendments, examination is based on actual amendments; if matters are only disclosed in the written argument (not in amendment) indicating requirements are met, examiner may re-notify the same ground at his/her discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written arguments and supporting documents are not part of specification
rubrics_metrics.description: A written argument or other documents including experiment results in response to the notice of the grounds for rejection shall not be a part of the specification of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, as these documents are submitted to clarify or verify matters in the description of the invention, an examiner may refer to them to decide patentability; written arguments submitted after the designated period may still be admitted for reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of multiple amendments — pre- and post-revision rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Where multiple amendments are submitted voluntarily before any notice of the ground for rejection, each amendment is accumulatively reflected on the specification to be examined. For applications filed before June 30, 2013 (pre-revision), multiple amendments submitted within the designated period are accumulatively reflected; for applications filed after July 1, 2013 (post-revision), where multiple amendments are submitted to a ground within the designated period, all amendments submitted before the final amendment are deemed withdrawn and the final specification to be examined is reflected only with the lastly-submitted amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A full-text amendment replaces the final specification to be examined. If an amendment in response to a final rejection is refused to be entered pursuant to Article 52(1), the amendment is treated as never submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional matters on amendment timing and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Voluntary amendments submitted before examination starts and amendments in response to a non-final rejection within the designated period are recognized as submitted; however, for post-2013 applications, where amendments to the ground for rejection are submitted more than twice within the designated period, earlier amendments before the final amendment are deemed withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant may voluntary-amend during the period between delivery and receipt of the grounds for rejection; if a written amendment identifies the delivery number of the notice, notification delivery is regarded earlier than amendment submission. Examination outcomes after amendment: (a) if no ground discovered -> grant; (b) if prior-notified ground remains -> reject; (c) if previously-notified grounds are overcome but a new ground generated by amendment or an unnotified pre-existing ground found -> re-notify non-final ground; for multiple amendments a & b, if a new ground arises from amendment b the examiner shall notify a final rejection necessitated by amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for documents and types of documents examiners may ask for
rubrics_metrics.description: If considered necessary to expedite examination, an examiner may ask an applicant to submit documents and other references required for examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical requested documents include: related documents and translations for international applications; examination outcomes in other patent offices; a written statement mapping each claim's technical subject matter to description paragraph numbers; a statement explaining relations among claims when many; a written gist summary of claimed invention; samples or experiment results where needed to verify effects (only if they'd confirm sufficiency upon filing); statements explaining formula induction or definitions of technical terms; statements clarifying claims in written arguments; documents relevant to examination results of priority-claim applications and their Korean translation. Requests should specify which document and are made under the examiner's name; submission period falls within period for written argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use, handling, storage and return/disposal of submitted documents/samples
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents submitted by an examiner's request are only used for reference material and cannot substitute or supplement the description. When receiving documents or samples, an examiner shall keep a document list and store them in a file wrapper if possible or store separately till examination closes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must store submitted items undamaged, pay attention on return requests, commence return procedure right after examination closes, designate return period and notify submitter; if no return request or submitter fails to retrieve within designated period, Commissioner may decide disposal. Documents submitted are reference only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of evidential documents as prior art and examination of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Where evidential documents submitted are periodicals or their copies, or copies of description or drawing(s) published before the application date, an examiner may use them as prior art without additional examination of evidence. For other documents, an examiner may use them as prior art only if confident of the fact to be verified without examination of evidence; if an applicant argues existence of the evidential fact in the written argument, examiner shall not admit the fact unless justifiable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the Patent Act has no provisions regarding an examination of evidence during examination, examiners should not reject an application based on evidential documents (other than periodicals/copies) when the evidential fact cannot be confirmed with confidence. Anyone (except an incompetent minor without legal rep) may provide evidence to an examiner arguing that an application shall not be patented; examiners may refer to group/association submissions instead of invalidating or returning them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances requiring additional search
rubrics_metrics.description: During the examination stage, an examiner shall conduct additional searches where: (1) incomplete understanding of claimed invention found via written argument, personal interview, or information; (2) amended claims include subject matters not covered by original search; (3) claimed invention excluded from original search due to lack of unity of invention; (4) an international patent application enters domestic stage and its translation is expected; (5) other cases considered necessary for additional research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional searches are required to ensure proper examination when scope or understanding changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination deferral or extension of processing period — grounds and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may defer an examination or extend the processing period within 2 months when an application falls under specified cases, noting deferral/extension is not allowed when Commissioner or examiner designates the processing period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grounds include: (i) prior-filed or conflicting applications not laid open or examination requests not made; (ii) period for domestic priority claim not elapsed; (iii) a patent trial or proceeding related to the application is pending (including administrative trial/litigation); (iv) required time due to outsourcing prior-art search, expert opinions, or consultation examination; (v) period for submission of evidential documents for priority right not elapsed; (vi) other necessary occasions. Deferral/extension must be reported to head and notified to applicant. Examiner must review >1/month whether reasons have been resolved and must conduct examination once reasons cleared by termination date. Further deferrals/extensions require reporting and are limited to two months except certain external-cause cases where extension allowed only for causes not imputable to the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling later-filed applications vs prior-filed applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Where more than two patent applications are filed on the identical invention, the examiner shall defer examination for later-filed applications until the prior-filed application has been processed or laid-open or registered. However, where the later-filed application can be rejected based on the same ground as the prior-filed application, the examiner can start examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If prior-filed application is processed/laid-open/registered after deferral, examiner may conduct examination on later-filed application but final decision must apply Article 36(1) once claim scope of prior-filed application is determined. Table in guideline explains procedures depending on disclosure and identity of applicants.
